ecological_hypothesis: Rainfall-associated chorus activation is thermally gated: recent-rain contrasts should produce stronger dry=0 -> wet CallingIndex 2-3 activation when the two matched surveys occur under warmer overall thermal conditions.
thermal_context: pair_mean_temp_c = mean of the wet-run and dry-run mean stop temperatures; z-score across the frozen pair sample.
primary_response: strong_new_score = sum wet CallingIndex for cells dry=0 and wet in {2,3}.
primary_model: strong_new_score ~ rain_contrast * pair_mean_temp_z + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + State + RunNumber, route-clustered covariance.
sensitivities: Repeat on new_ci3_count (dry=0 -> wet CI3 full chorus).
Repeat the primary model on same-observer + physical-stop stable pairs.
Fit descriptive State random-rain-slope models with and without the interaction and report change in state-slope SD; no reduction threshold is a pass gate.
interpretation: Support would identify temperature as a moderator of the rainfall association, not a physiological mediator.
A null interaction would weaken a simple warm-gated explanation for state heterogeneity.
Pair mean temperature is observational and can covary with seasonal ecology despite State and RunNumber adjustment.
No causal rainfall or temperature claim is authorized.
